title: James Webb Space Telescope — built at L2

subject.summary: The deployed James Webb Space Telescope drifting at Sun-Earth L2, assembled in eight stages: spacecraft bus, power and comms, sunshield rigging, the five membranes, the OTE tower and backplane, the eighteen gold hexagons, and finally the secondary mirror on its three struts. Published dimensions (21.197 x 14.162 m shield, 6.5 m aperture, 1.32 m segments, 0.74 m secondary, 0.6 m antenna) are cited; the arrangement of masses, the bus envelope and the tower heights are reconstructed from the reference renders and blueprint.

identity.feature: Eighteen gold hexagonal segments tiling a 6.6 m aperture with the AOS at the centre
Five-layer sunshield, 21.2 m x 14.2 m, pointed at both ends and fanned at the corners
Secondary mirror standing 7.4 m ahead on three long struts
Sun-side bus with the five-panel solar array and the 0.6 m antenna

next: the five membranes are still the emptiest surface: bow each catenary 0.15-0.2 m below the plane and scallop the border between tie points
the four sunshield corners read as stepped tabs, not the fan of membrane panels the references show
the bus and ISIM want real blanket/louver detail; they are still plain boxes at close range
the ceremony's 0.9 s ghost preview is the reason the assembly sheet reads backwards; drop interference for a strict build order
the secondary dish still reads as a spoked wheel up close: give it a smooth paraboloid with a rim bezel
no gold tint is possible in this palette (the renderer owns colour); the mirror reads as light plates, not gold
